searchText: New channel aimed to discuss the current merge interop specs (http://interop.merge.wiki/) as well as all the fun practical engineering problems we're about to run into 🏺 Implementing the engine API I wonder what should the consensus client do if: - calls prepare_payload and gets parent unknown. Who will resolve the situation? Will the execution client find that block on its own? Or is the consensus client expected to provide it? - calls prepare_payload and gets status syncing. For how long should the consensus client wait and do nothing? Should it keep attempting to do stuff and hitting the "is syncing" brick wall? - calls forkchoice_updated and execution client hasn't received the consensus validated status. Should the consensus client call consensus_validated, then retry forkchoice_updated? Or could the execution client just assume that any route in forkchoice_updated call params + prepare_payload is consensus_validated? test <pjickling> test works Is any execution client ready to start some early interop testing following the latest spec? Looking at doing some preliminary testing tomorrow For consensus-layer clients, we suggest using the test vectors from the recently released v1.1.0. It does not substantively change merge specs but does add additional vectors Was looking at testing the engine API side-effects, fork mechanics, etc <sigpaul> Are you referring to consensus-specs v1.1.0.beta.5? (re @amphora_interop_bot: <djrtwo>For consensus-layer clients, we suggest using the test vectors from the recently released v1.1.0. It does not substantively change merge specs but does add additional vectors) <dannyryan> beta.5 is the “interop target” <dannyryan> but we just released v1.1.0 for altair mainnet <dannyryan> this also included additional merge vectors and did not change the merge spec <dannyryan> so I suggest utilizing those vectors for better coverage <sigpaul> Got it, thanks
